name: White Rabbit PTP Core software (wrpc-sw)
summary: Software for the White Rabbit PTP Core (WRPC): a bare-metal PTP daemon (PPSi) and drivers for the WRPC HDL that runs on a soft CPU inside the FPGA, giving a node sub-ns sync over fibre.
why_it_matters: The node side of White Rabbit: if a team has a WR-capable FPGA board, this is what turns it into a synchronised timing endpoint.
hackathon_notes: Needs WR hardware (e.g. SPEC board + WR switch) and the wr-cores gateware. Not a 48 h starting point without the kit on the table; useful as reference for how WR extends PTP with phase tracking and link calibration.

name: White Rabbit (OHWR project hub)
summary: Umbrella OHWR project for White Rabbit, the deterministic Ethernet extension of PTP; the wiki collects specs, hardware lists, user stories and links to all WR sub-projects.
why_it_matters: Starting point to find which WR hardware, gateware and calibration notes exist before committing to WR in a timing demo.
hackathon_notes: Read the wiki, not the code. Use it to pick hardware and to cite WR accuracy from the project's own docs.

name: White Rabbit calibration
summary: Procedures and notes for calibrating White Rabbit equipment: fixed hardware delays and fibre asymmetry that must be measured for absolute time accuracy.
why_it_matters: Calibration is where path asymmetry gets removed in practice; the same A/2 error modelled in sample:timing-network-holdover.
hackathon_notes: Reference reading for explaining why uncalibrated asymmetry biases two-way time transfer.

name: Roughenough
summary: Rust Roughtime (RFC 10049) server and client with a batching UDP server, optional malfeasance reporting and several key-protection backends (KMS, PKCS#11, SSH agent).
why_it_matters: Quickest way to stand up an authenticated rough-time source and a client that checks several servers against each other.
hackathon_notes: cargo build needs a recent Rust (README states MSRV 1.94.1). Run a local server plus public servers; show the client flagging a server whose time you skew.

name: pyroughtime
summary: Python Roughtime library and CLI implementing RFC 10049; validates signatures against server long-term keys, queries several servers to catch a misbehaving one, and includes a small test server.
why_it_matters: Python is the fastest route to put Roughtime into a hackathon notebook or detector.
hackathon_notes: pip install pycryptodome in the venv. Query several servers, then run the bundled test server with a wrong clock to show detection.

name: ntpperf
summary: Load generator for NTP servers and PTP masters by chrony's author: simulates many clients with raw Ethernet frames via libpcap and reports responses, losses and, with a known direct link, how transmit timestamp accuracy degrades with rate.
why_it_matters: Tests whether a time server stays accurate under request floods - a denial-of-service angle on timing infrastructure.
hackathon_notes: Needs a dedicated link and routing so responses come back to the test host. Lab tool, not demo material.

name: flashptpd
summary: Experimental C++17 client/server style PTP from Meinberg: the client sends Sync with a request TLV and the server answers, so no BMCA or master announce is needed. Archived.
why_it_matters: Shows a unicast request/response PTP variant close to NTP in shape; useful when thinking about how a client chooses among several servers.
hackathon_notes: Archived; read for the protocol idea, do not build on it.

name: ptp-book
summary: Open book on PTP (IEEE 1588 / gPTP) in Chinese with an English translation: BMCA, the four-timestamp maths, transparent clocks, hardware timestamping, security, a walk through linuxptp source, and a ~1000-line ptp-lite implementation.
why_it_matters: Fast self-study path for a team member who has to explain or modify PTP during the event.
hackathon_notes: Read the English chapters for BMCA and the servo; ptp-lite is small enough to instrument for a delay-attack demo.

name: LibPTP
summary: OMNeT++/INET library for simulating IEEE 1588-2008 networks: ordinary, boundary and transparent clocks, E2E and P2P delay, a PI servo with pluggable servos and filters, and power-law clock noise via LibPLN.
why_it_matters: A packet-level PTP network simulator if a stdlib model is too coarse.
hackathon_notes: OMNeT++ setup is heavy and the repo was last pushed in 2021. Prefer sample:timing-network-holdover or clknetsim unless packet-level detail is required.

name: flexPTP
summary: PTP (IEEE 1588, also 802.1AS) for Cortex-M4/M7 microcontrollers: master and slave ordinary clock, E2E and P2P, L2 and L4 transports, one- and two-step. MIT licence, with a journal paper.
why_it_matters: Puts PTP on the MCU next to a sensor, so each sensor node timestamps in a shared timebase.
hackathon_notes: Needs an MCU with an Ethernet MAC that supports PTP timestamps (STM32F7/H7 class). Good fit for a sensor-network TDOA demo if the boards are at hand.

name: Wi-PTP
summary: PTP over Wi-Fi: a patched ath9k driver (Linux 4.19) that timestamps in the Wi-Fi hardware path plus an adjusted linuxptp.
why_it_matters: Time sync between drones or ground nodes over Wi-Fi instead of cable.
hackathon_notes: Needs Atheros ath9k cards and a kernel rebuild on an old kernel. Cite the idea; do not plan on building it in 48 h.

name: linuxptp-daemon (OpenShift)
summary: Kubernetes DaemonSet that manages ptp4l, phc2sys, ts2phc and timemaster per node, parses their logs into clock-state events, and for u-blox GNSS grandmasters treats a UBX-NAV-STATUS spoofing flag as GNSS loss.
why_it_matters: Production code that already wires GNSS spoofing detection into PTP grandmaster state - a concrete reference for clock-state handling and holdover.
hackathon_notes: Read pkg/parser and the ts2phc monitoring code for log parsing and state machines; reuse the regexes to parse your own ptp4l logs. Running it needs OpenShift and E810-class NICs.

name: time-transfer-tools
summary: MATLAB classes to read CGGTTS (V1, V2E) and RINEX 2/3 observation files, match observations between two stations and compute averaged differences - the GNSS common-view time transfer workflow.
why_it_matters: Lets a team compare two GNSS-timed sites the way timing labs do.
hackathon_notes: Needs MATLAB. Useful only if CGGTTS files are available (e.g. from a timing lab).

name: gr-allan
summary: GNU Radio sink block that wraps allantools to plot Allan deviation in real time from a stream.
why_it_matters: Live ADEV of an SDR-measured frequency or phase offset during a demo.
hackathon_notes: Tested by the author on GNU Radio 3.10.5; needs allantools installed. Build with cmake.

name: GNSSTimeServer
summary: ESP8266/ESP32 stratum-1 time server fed by a GNSS module and a TCXO-backed RTC, serving NTP and RDATE over WiFi or W5500 Ethernet, with a PTPv2 master edition, web dashboard and battery backup.
why_it_matters: Cheapest portable GNSS-fed time source for a field demo network.
hackathon_notes: Bill of materials and firmware in the repo; an ESP32 plus GNSS module with PPS. Accuracy is MCU-class, not NIC hardware timestamping.

name: MMCM_GPSDO
summary: All-digital GPSDO in VHDL for a Basys3 FPGA board: steers the clock with MMCM phase shifts from a GPS 1PPS, showing frequency error on LEDs. Author describes the loop as simple and constants as empirical.
why_it_matters: Minimal FPGA disciplining loop to read or extend with holdover logic.
hackathon_notes: Needs a Basys3 (Artix-7) and a GPS with PPS. No licence file per GitHub metadata - read, do not copy.
